comparison: Both evaluate the Yki-Ncoa6 interaction data (C2, C22-C28, C91-C94). OpenEval finds the biochemical evidence SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY due to Reviewer 1's conceptual concern about how nuclear Ncoa6 promotes cytoplasmic Yorkie translocation. Peer review also includes nuclear localization claims (C29, C95-C98) that OpenEval addresses separately in R2.

OpenEval R2 evaluates nuclear localization data (C29, C95-C98) as SUPPORTED based on immunofluorescence. Peer R1 includes these same claims but rates them UNCERTAIN due to the mechanistic question about how nuclear Ncoa6 affects cytoplasmic Yki. This represents a key disagreement on interpretation of the localization data.

Both evaluate luciferase reporter assays (C31-C33, C99-C100). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as functional evidence linking interaction to transcriptional output. Peer review also finds these SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 noting that 'Ncoa6 addition increases the ability of Yki to promote activation of a transcriptional reporter.' Strong agreement.

Both evaluate ChIP data showing Yki and Ncoa6 enrichment at diap1 HRE (C34-C35, C101). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as direct evidence of Ncoa6 recruitment to target genes. Peer review also finds this SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 noting enrichment 'at the diap1 HRE.' Strong agreement.

Both evaluate wing disc RNAi experiments (C3-C4, C36-C38, C40-C41, C102-C103, C105). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as direct in vivo evidence. Peer review also finds these SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 noting 'knockdown of Ncoa6 with RNAi via dppGal4 leads to a suppression of growth' and target gene reduction. Peer review notes minor concern about non-autonomy in fj expression but accepts core findings. Strong agreement with minor interpretive differences.

Both evaluate eye genetic interaction data (C42-C46, C107-C116). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as consistent genetic interactions showing Ncoa6 as positive regulator. Peer review also finds these SUPPORTED, stating 'Genetic interaction screens in the eye support a role for Ncoa6 in growth control via the Hippo pathway.' Strong agreement.

Both evaluate MARCM clone epistasis experiments (C47-C49, C118-C119, C121). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED, demonstrating Ncoa6 acts downstream/parallel to Hpo. Peer review rates these UNCERTAIN, noting reviewers explicitly requested these experiments, suggesting initial data may have been insufficient or added in revision. Disagreement on sufficiency of evidence.

Both evaluate SdDB-Ncoa6 fusion rescue experiments (C5-C6, C51-C57, C123-C125). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as critical evidence that Yki's primary function is recruiting Ncoa6. Peer review also finds these SUPPORTED, describing the fusion protein growth effect and Diap1 upregulation. Peer review notes minor concern about edge effects in clones but accepts main finding. Strong agreement with minor interpretive differences.

OpenEval R9 evaluates luciferase data for SdDB-Ncoa6 fusion (C58, C126) as SUPPORTED, showing bypass of Wts regulation. Peer R6 includes these claims in broader evaluation of fusion protein experiments, finding them SUPPORTED. Agreement on this complementary evidence.

OpenEval R10 evaluates parallel Trr RNAi experiments (C59-C66 and supporting claims) as SUPPORTED, noting one exception (C64, C114) where Trr RNAi doesn't suppress Wts RNAi. Peer R3 includes some Trr wing disc data (C59-C61, C104, C106) in broader evaluation of RNAi experiments, finding them SUPPORTED. Partial overlap with agreement.

OpenEval R10 includes Trr genetic interactions in eye (C62-C64, C108, C111, C114, C117) as part of comprehensive Trr evaluation, finding them SUPPORTED despite one exception. Peer R4 includes these same Trr eye interaction claims in evaluation of genetic screens, finding them SUPPORTED. Agreement on Trr involvement in Hippo signaling.

OpenEval R10 includes Trr epistasis data (C65-C66, C120, C122) showing Trr RNAi suppresses hpo mutant phenotypes. Peer R5 includes these claims in evaluation of epistasis experiments rated UNCERTAIN, suggesting reviewers initially found this evidence insufficient. Disagreement on sufficiency.

Both evaluate ChIP-qPCR data on H3K4me1/me3 at target genes (C7, C77-C85, C127-C128). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as strong mechanistic evidence. Peer review also finds these SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 stating data are 'consistent with the author's model.' Reviewer suggests additional experiment with dSet1 but notes it's 'not necessary for publication.' Strong agreement.

Both evaluate immunofluorescence data on global H3K4 methylation levels (C70-C73, C129-C132). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as important controls showing gene-specific rather than global effects. Peer review also finds these SUPPORTED without challenge. Perfect claim overlap and strong agreement.

OpenEval R13 evaluates the synthesized mechanistic model (C86) as SUPPORTED based on multiple lines of evidence. Peer R7 evaluates the H3K4 methylation data supporting this model as SUPPORTED and 'consistent with the author's model.' Agreement on the mechanistic interpretation, though peer review focuses on specific data while OpenEval explicitly evaluates the integrated model.

OpenEval evaluates the initial screen identification of Ncoa6 (C21) as SUPPORTED based on screen data and validation experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim about the screen methodology.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about COMPASS-like complex composition (C1, C12-C13, C16) as SUPPORTED by prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/context claims.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about H3K4 methylation patterns at enhancers and promoters (C67-C69, C74-C76) as SUPPORTED by prior literature and Figure 6A. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background/context claims (C8-C11, C14-C15, C17-C20, C23-C24, C39, C50, C87-C90) as SUPPORTED by appropriate citations to established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims, as peer review focuses on novel experimental findings.

OpenEval evaluates independent validation of Yki-Ncoa6 interaction from prior work (C30, citing Kwon et al., 2013) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific citation-based claim.
